concepts.def: Forced separation of people by race or class
US laws enforcing racial segregation in the South
The right to vote in political elections
South Africa's 1948-94 system of racial separation
Peaceful refusal to obey unjust laws
1909 US group fighting for African American rights

walkthroughs.body_html:
In Britain the Suffragettes from 1903 used militant protest — speeches, smashing windows, hunger strikes.

In 1918 women over 30 with property won the vote. In 1928 it became equal to men's at age 21.

From the 1950s African Americans challenged Jim Crow laws.

Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in 1955. The Montgomery Bus Boycott followed. Martin Luther King Jr led peaceful marches and gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963.

From 1948 South Africa's government enforced apartheid — separating people by race in housing, schools and voting.

Nelson Mandela led the African National Congress (ANC). He was jailed for 27 years and released in 1990. Apartheid ended officially in 1994.

mcqs.q: Who refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery in 1955?

numericals.q: In which year did apartheid officially end in South Africa?
numericals.hint: Nelson Mandela was elected President that year.

free_texts.q: What is the term for peaceful refusal to obey unjust laws? Two words. (lowercase)
free_texts.hint: Civil + a word meaning 'not obeying'. Used by Gandhi and MLK.
